# Memdoor

> The headless-first coding agent, open source, on your own API key. One gateway, every door: Every run is a conversation on a gateway on your machine, started from a terminal window, `memdoor run` in a script or CI, a cron schedule, your editor or your phone, and opened live from any of them. Steps run as a checked, resumable graph with a gate for you; a decision model cuts what the model reads. One binary, free; Pro is $10 a month for what runs on memdoor.ai.

## What it is

Memdoor reads your files, writes patches, runs the build and fixes what it broke, in the directory you launch it from (`memdoor tui`). The window is one door among several onto the same gateway: `memdoor run "<prompt>"` is one headless turn (prompt in, answer on stdout, exit code 0 checked / 2 unverified or a failing check / 3 it needed you), `memdoor workflow run <name> --wait` a workflow from a shell or CI, `memdoor cron add` a schedule, `memdoor acp` the editor, `/remote` the phone, and `memdoor resume <id>` opens any of those runs in a window, live, with the same session underneath. Guide: https://memdoor.ai/docs/headless Every model call is on your own account: OpenRouter, Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, DeepSeek, Baseten, Groq, xAI or a company AI gateway (`memdoor connect`, or export the key). Memdoor adds nothing to the bill and your code does not pass through memdoor.ai.

A decision model (Jev, by TypeSafe — a hosted model, not a local one) sits in front of the chat model and answers typed questions with a calibrated probability in under half a second. The excerpts being judged go to it, through OpenRouter on your OpenRouter key or directly on a decision key (`memdoor connect typesafe`); on an Anthropic, OpenAI or Gemini key alone it is off and the agent works without the savings. Every host the binary can contact: https://memdoor.ai/docs/security. The harness acts on the answers:

- Judged reads: search hits, file sections and log lines are scored against the task; only what counts reaches the model.
- A toolbox sized to the turn: only the tools the request needs are sent (schemas were 37% of an edit turn's input when measured).
- A stop instead of a cap: a turn that stops making progress ends with what it has.
- `/model` pins any tool-capable model of a connected provider at its list price.

Measured over 44 paired runs (same tasks, decisions off and on, alternating): 22 of 22 passed each way; a question about the codebase went from 54,661 to 14,367 input tokens (−74%, three pairs); tasks that read the same files either way (an edit with a test, ten one-file fixes) changed nothing, within ±11%. Table: https://github.com/guregodevo/memdoor/blob/main/docs/features/DECIDE.md

## Workflows

Describe the steps and the coder writes a workflow: one YAML per task in `.memdoor/workflows/<name>/steps/`, run as a DAG by mario. Task kinds: `command` (a shell line; its exit code is the proof), `llm` (one model call), `agent` (a turn of the coder). Independent tasks run in parallel. A task is done when its target exists (a file, a command that exits 0); a target already true is skipped. An `external: true` task is a gate: the run waits until a person approves (`a` in /workflow, `memdoor workflow approve <run> <task>`). A failed run resumes at the failed step. `memdoor cron add --workflow <name>` runs one on your local cron. The catalog at /workflows lists workflows that exist as files and have run, each with a recording: ship, review, tui-check, issue-to-pr, release-check, digest, karpathy-recipe.

## Remote control (Pro)

`/remote` in the TUI prints a link and a QR code. The page it opens on a phone is the terminal itself, running on your computer; screen and keystrokes are end-to-end encrypted, the relay on memdoor.ai forwards what it cannot read. `/remote off` revokes the link.

## Price

- Free: the agent, the decision model (on an OpenRouter key or a decision key) and workflows with local schedules, on your own key.
- Pro, $10/month: remote control through the memdoor.ai relay, and every workflow run's state kept on memdoor.ai, one table per workspace, so a workflow can wait on a task another workflow produced, from any machine; `memdoor workflow history` answers from anywhere. Coming: runs with the laptop closed. A seat never supplies a model key. https://memdoor.ai/pricing or `memdoor account subscribe`.
- Enterprise: the hosted state and the relay served for a company on its own instance or host, people and admins set up by us, invoiced. hello@memdoor.ai.

## Install

```
curl -fsSL https://memdoor.ai/install.sh | bash
export OPEN_ROUTER_API_KEY=sk-or-...
cd your-project && memdoor tui
```

Windows: `irm https://memdoor.ai/install.ps1 | iex`
